findings.issue: The optional public-tenant branch wraps `this.validator.validate(...)` in a catch-all that returns true (lines ~52-57). `packages/backend/src/auth/auth-context.guard.ts` does the same around `tokenVerifier.verifyAuthorizationHeader` (`catch { return true; }`). `StynxJwtValidator` throws plain `Error`s for infrastructure failures such as 'Failed to load STYNX JWKS: <status>', 'No STYNX JWKS source configured' and fetch rejections. `CognitoTokenVerifier` lets jose/JWKS network errors propagate. So during a JWKS or verifier outage, a valid bearer on an `optionalAuth` route is quietly downgraded to the nominal public actor. The contract `docs/framework/contracts/tenancy-context-1.5.md` §UPS-TEN-02/03 says 'Session lookup or verifier infrastructure failures are not silently treated as revoked or invalid credentials', and DETRAN UPS-TEN-03 says a valid Authorization must follow the authenticated flow. Only session-lookup and permission-cache failures propagate today.
findings.required_change: Engineer: in both guards, separate credential rejection (bad signature, issuer, audience, expiry, malformed or absent) from verifier infrastructure failure (JWKS fetch or configuration errors), for example with a typed invalid-credential error or error class from the validator and verifier. Only the credential-rejection case should fall back to the nominal actor; rethrow everything else. Inspector: add sensors for both guards where the verifier throws an infrastructure error and the request fails instead of returning 200 with the nominal actor. Architect: rebind `law/trace.json`. If the Architect wants catch-all instead, the contract sentence has to change first.

findings.issue: Several StynxAuthGuard sensors that cycle-1 and the contract Verification boundary require are still missing. (1) Revoked session on `optionalAuth`: cycle-1 finding 9 asked for a sensor, but the only `activeSession: false` case (line ~117) is the protected-route 401. No test pins that a verified token whose `sessionService.get(sid)` returns null leaves the actor nominal with no `stynxClaims`, principal or verified marker. (2) Upstream identity: the invalid/absent test starts from `{ headers: {} }`, and nothing seeds principal, `stynxClaims`, user, actor, tenantId or `verifiedSessionId` before `StynxAuthGuard` runs. Only AuthContextGuard has that test (`packages/backend/test/unit/auth-context.guard.spec.ts`). The clearing code exists but is unproven for the guard that feeds PermissionGuard. (3) No test shows the verified grant for a public tenant route with `@Permission`, where a real `StynxAuthGuard`-verified principal holding the permission passes PermissionGuard. Existing tests only cover nominal denial with mocked reflectors.
findings.required_change: Inspector: add these tests. (a) An `optionalAuth` request with a validator-accepted token and a null session gives nominal actorId and tenant over HTTP in `auth-context-public-tenant.integration.spec.ts`, plus a unit assertion that none of the identity fields or the verified marker are set. (b) A request pre-seeded with principal, `stynxClaims`, user, actor, tenantId, `verifiedSessionId`, `verifiedTenantClaim` and `verifiedTenantEntitlement`, with absent and with invalid bearer, has all of them removed by `StynxAuthGuard`. (c) An HTTP route with `@UseGuards(StynxAuthGuard, PermissionGuard)`, `@PublicTenantRoute({optionalAuth:true})` and `@Permission('records:read')` returns 200 for a verified member holding the permission and 403 'Missing permission records:read' for nominal and invalid tokens. Architect: rebind `law/trace.json`.

findings.issue: The test swaps core and tenancy import order, but it never asserts that the APP_INTERCEPTOR execution order actually flipped. It also uses a supplied X-Request-Id, so a second context opened by an interceptor would reuse the same ID and still pass. The guard reads `requestId` but doesn't record it for comparison.
findings.required_change: Inspector: record the guard-read requestId and compare it with the handler and response values on a request without X-Request-Id, so a generated ID must be identical across all three. Also assert the observed interceptor order for each variant, for example with probe interceptors or by inspecting `app.getGlobalInterceptors`/the config order.

findings.issue: The interceptor derives `publicTenantOptionalAuth` from route metadata itself and then treats `request.stynxClaims?.sub ?? request.principal?.id` as the verified actor. If neither STYNX guard ran (a custom guard or middleware), any upstream-populated principal is accepted as the actor once membership passes. The damage is bounded by the Host tenant and the membership check.
findings.required_change: Architect/Engineer: only treat a principal or claims as verified when a STYNX guard-owned provenance marker is present (for example a symbol set by StynxAuthGuard or AuthContextGuard). Otherwise use the nominal actor. Alternatively, document that a STYNX auth guard is required on optionalAuth routes.

findings.issue: The public-route host-claim comparison reads only `principal.claims.tenant_id`/`tenantId`. `CognitoTokenVerifier` puts tenant claims in `custom:tenant_id`, `https://stynx.dev/tenant` or `tenants` (principal.tenants), so a Cognito token for tenant B under Host A gets no `TENANCY:CONFLICT:host-claim` and is only gated by membership. This fails safe because Host still selects the tenant, but it doesn't match the contract's host-claim wording.
findings.required_change: Architect: define which verified claim counts as the tenant claim for AuthContextGuard. Engineer: derive `verifiedTenantClaim` from that definition, for example the configured tenant claims or a single-entry principal.tenants. Inspector: add a Cognito-shaped conflict case.

summary: Most cycle-1 repairs are real, but two blocking gaps remain, so the verdict is REVIEW, not PASS. The code no longer lets a JWKS or verifier outage be distinguished from a bad token, which breaks the contract's no-silent-downgrade rule, and StynxAuthGuard still lacks the revoked-session, cleared-upstream-identity and verified-permission-grant tests. What is repaired, checked against code and tests: (1) Both import orders run over real Nest and PostgreSQL with a guard reading context before the interceptors (`tenancy-context-order.integration.spec.ts`), though order flipping and single-ID generation aren't asserted. (2) The real AuthContextGuard and real StynxAuthGuard run with tenancy over HTTP for absent, invalid, null, conflict, outsider and member cases (`auth-context-public-tenant.integration.spec.ts`). (3) Middleware X-Request-Id gives a 400 body, two transitive core imports give one ID, auth-only and backend-only apps propagate sid, the configured `X-Portal-Tenant` conflict returns the exact body, and upper-case UUIDs are accepted. (4) Entitlement allow/deny/throw is enforced after Host selection. (5) `global: true` is removed and recorded in the contract. (6) Audit reads as stynx_app return the row under A and nothing under B. (7) Handler discovery now walks the prototype chain, with inherited-handler tests for both packages. Legacy `@Public()` plus `@Permission` stays permissive, `@System` can't bypass the public-tenant permission check, and `@ReadOnly` is set on both branches (unit test only). Commits are role-separated (Engineer: src, scripts, changeset; Inspector: tests only; Architect: law, docs, baselines), and no test was weakened; the removed lines only tightened assertions. `pnpm check:trace` reports 393/393. The CI log shows api-baseline 44/44, rls-negative OK, and the new suites passing. The changeset covers the fixed group as minor, and no DETRAN code was copied.
